key_insight: Dynamically routing queries across language model instances can adjust datacenter power demand without deferring requests.
engineering_relevance: Query routing offers a software-level mechanism for grid-responsive power management while maintaining service for interactive workloads.
method: Model how query arrival rates and sequence lengths affect token iteration time, request residence time, serving capacity, and power.
Characterize feasible routing allocations and their achievable power flexibility.
Select routing strategies to achieve desired power consumption behavior.
evidence_signal: Validation across four GPU platforms and 1B–70B models yielded 2.8% mean absolute percentage error in estimated flexibility; a trace-driven simulation of 10,000 H100 GPUs showed up to 16% power flexibility, achieving 90% of the desired reduction in approximately 10 seconds.
watch_item: Datacenter-scale results are simulation-based; production deployment should verify response times and interactive service performance under changing workloads.
paper_title: Creating Power Flexibility in Datacenters via Query Routing
